name: Promenade Chassé
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the chassé after the Whisk, travelling in promenade, with a full lift onto the toes as the feet come together on the half beat; the couple stays in promenade and turns to face in the next figure (an Open Natural Turn). Named after the American-style Promenade Chassé, which stays in promenade; the International Chassé from Promenade Position has the follow turn to face during the chassé instead. Timing 1, 2 & 3. Starts in crossed promenade and travels towards the open side of the V: diagonally forward left for the lead (facing 315), diagonally forward right for the follow (facing 225), so due -x in the figure's frame. Count 1: the lead's right foot forward and across, 0.5. Count 2: the crossed foot comes from behind to land 0.4 past the other along the line of travel (written per partner because they come from opposite sides: 0.9 forward and 0.7 across). &: close, taking weight late. Count 3: 0.4 along the line again. Sizes as the other waltz figures (0.5 first step, side steps 0.4), agreed by the owner. Rise: 'a full lift onto toes' written as 0.1 (the model only has a height), 0.06 by the end of 2, 0.1 on &, lowering through 3. The model moves rise evenly across each step, so the lowering is spread over count 3 rather than coming at its end. Ends still in promenade with the feet apart, lead on his left; not a named stance, so expectEnd lists the feet.
